metadata.question: Did the Central Valley of California have a higher water height equivalent in October 2022 than March 2023?

data.raw_code: 1. Search strategy: Use GRACE/GRACE-FO equivalent water thickness (EWT) over the Central Valley polygon. Monthly windows: 2022-10-01 to 2022-11-01 and 2023-03-01 to 2023-04-01. Try a list of candidate GRACE datasets, pick the first that returns data. 2. Masking strategy: No cloud masking needed (GRACE is not optical). Use land-only product; ocean is masked by default. 3. Logic: Validate image collections non-empty (else C1), check valid pixel count after masking (C2), verify mean result is not None/NaN and within a plausible range (C3). Compare means: if Oct > Mar then A else B. ```python import ee import math try: ee.Initialize(project='earthsense-436113') except Exception as e: ee.Initialize() # 1. Geometry & Time Definitions # Approximate Central Valley bounding polygon geom = ee.Geometry.Polygon( [[[-122.8, 34.8], [-118.7, 34.8], [-118.7, 40.9], [-122.8, 40.9], [-122.8, 34.8]]], None, False ) periods = { 'Oct2022': ('2022-10-01', '2022-11-01'), 'Mar2023': ('2023-03-01', '2023-04-01'), } # Candidate GRACE/GRACE-FO datasets (try in order) candidates = [ {'id': 'NASA/GRACE/MASS_GRIDS/LAND', 'band': 'lwe_thickness'}, # Additional plausible IDs (may fail; caught safely) {'id': 'JPL/GRACE_GRACE-FO/MASCON_CRI_GRID_RL06', 'band': 'lwe_thickness'}, {'id': 'JPL/GRACE/MASS_GRIDS/CRI', 'band': 'lwe_thickness'}, ] scale_m = 100000 # coarse scale appropriate for GRACE, >= 1000 as required def get_period_stats(start, end): last_exception = None for cand in candidates: try: col = ee.ImageCollection(cand['id']).select(cand['band']).filterDate(start, end) # Global dataset; filterBounds is optional but harmless: col = col.filterBounds(geom) size = col.size().getInfo() except Exception as e: last_exception = e continue if size == 0: # Try slight widening (±7 days) to accommodate missing monthly release try: col2 = ee.ImageCollection(cand['id']).select(cand['band']) \ .filterDate(ee.Date(start).advance(-7, 'day'), ee.Date(end).advance(7, 'day')) \ .filterBounds(geom) size2 = col2.size().getInfo() except Exception as e: last_exception = e continue if size2 == 0: continue else: col = col2 size = size2 # Compute mean image over available scenes img = col.mean() # Count valid pixels in region try: count = img.reduceRegion( reducer=ee.Reducer.count(), geometry=geom, scale=scale_m, maxPixels=1e9, ).get(cand['band']).getInfo() except Exception as e: last_exception = e continue if (count is None) or (int(count) == 0): return {'error': 'C2', 'detail': f"No valid pixels after masking for {cand['id']} {start}..{end}"} # Mean LWE (cm) try: mean_val = img.reduceRegion( reducer=ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry=geom, scale=scale_m, maxPixels=1e9, ).get(cand['band']).getInfo() except Exception as e: last_exception = e continue # Validate mean if mean_val is None or (isinstance(mean_val, float) and (math.isnan(mean_val) or math.isinf(mean_val))): return {'error': 'C3', 'detail': f"Invalid mean (None/NaN/Inf) for {cand['id']} {start}..{end}"} # Plausibility check: GRACE LWE in cm typically within ±300 cm if isinstance(mean_val, (int, float)) and abs(mean_val) > 500: return {'error': 'C3', 'detail': f"Unrealistic LWE {mean_val} cm for {cand['id']}"} return { 'error': None, 'dataset': cand['id'], 'band': cand['band'], 'images': int(size), 'pixels': int(count), 'mean_cm': float(mean_val), } # If all candidates failed to load/compute if last_exception is not None: # If failures were due to empty collections only, treat as C1; otherwise D. # We conservatively return C1 if no images found; but here we couldn't even load. return {'error': 'C1', 'detail': 'No images found or datasets unavailable for the given dates.'} return {'error': 'C1', 'detail': 'No images found for the given dates.'} # 2-3. Data Acquisition, Processing, and Validation results = {} for key, (start, end) in periods.items(): results[key] = get_period_stats(start, end) # Handle error cases # If any period has an error, emit that code (priority order C1, C2, C3; else D would have been thrown earlier) for code in ['C1', 'C2', 'C3']: if any((results[k].get('error') == code) for k in results): # Print minimal diagnostics for k in results: r = results[k] if r.get('error'): print(f"{k}: ERROR {r['error']} - {r.get('detail','')}") else: print(f"{k}: Images={r['images']}, Mean(cm)={r['mean_cm']:.2f}, Pixels={r['pixels']}, Dataset={r['dataset']}") print(f"{code}") raise SystemExit(0) # 4. Calculation oct_mean = results['Oct2022']['mean_cm'] mar_mean = results['Mar2023']['mean_cm'] # 5. Output concise stats and final answer print(f"Oct 2022: Images={results['Oct2022']['images']}, Mean(cm)={oct_mean:.2f}, Pixels={results['Oct2022']['pixels']}, Dataset={results['Oct2022']['dataset']}") print(f"Mar 2023: Images={results['Mar2023']['images']}, Mean(cm)={mar_mean:.2f}, Pixels={results['Mar2023']['pixels']}, Dataset={results['Mar2023']['dataset']}") diff = oct_mean - mar_mean print(f"Diff (Oct - Mar)={diff:.2f} cm") # 6. Final Answer if oct_mean is None or mar_mean is None or any([math.isnan(oct_mean), math.isnan(mar_mean)]): print("C3") elif oct_mean > mar_mean: print("A") else: print("B") ```
